sanskrit.deva:
अथ हैनं शैब्यः सत्यकामः पप्रच्छ ।
स यो ह वै तद्भगवन्मनुष्येषु प्रायणान्तमोंकारमभिध्यायीत ।
कतमं वाव स तेन लोकं जयतीति ॥ १ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
atha hainaṃ śaibyaḥ satyakāmaḥ papraccha |
sa yo ha vai tad bhagavan manuṣyeṣu prāyaṇāntam oṃkāram abhidhyāyīta |
katamaṃ vāva sa tena lokaṃ jayatīti || 1 ||

lines.iast: atha hainaṃ śaibyaḥ satyakāmaḥ papraccha
sa yo ha vai tad bhagavan manuṣyeṣu prāyaṇāntam oṃkāram abhidhyāyīta
lines.deva: स यो ह वै तद्भगवन्मनुष्येषु प्रायणान्तमोंकारमभिध्यायीत

lines.iast: katamaṃ vāva sa tena lokaṃ jayatīti
lines.deva: कतमं वाव स तेन लोकं जयतीति

padaccheda.iast: atha ha enam śaibyaḥ satyakāmaḥ papraccha saḥ yaḥ ha vai tat bhagavan manuṣyeṣu prāyaṇa-antam oṃkāram abhidhyāyīta katamam vāva saḥ tena lokam jayati iti
padaccheda.deva: अथ ह एनम् शैब्यः सत्यकामः पप्रच्छ सः यः ह वै तत् भगवन् मनुष्येषु प्रायण-अन्तम् ओंकारम् अभिध्यायीत कतमम् वाव सः तेन लोकम् जयति इति

translations.text: Then Satyakāma Śaibya asked him: ‘Venerable sir, he among men who should meditate on the syllable Om until death, that wonder: which world does he win by it?’

notes: Śaṅkara, introducing the praśna: now the question is begun in order to enjoin the worship of Om as the means of reaching the higher and the lower Brahman.

Śaṅkara: tat: like a wonder. prāyaṇāntam: until death, that is, as long as he lives. abhidhyāyīta: should think on it, turned towards it: with the organs withdrawn from outer objects and the mind collected, having by devotion laid on Om the idea of Brahman. The word abhidhyāna means an unbroken stream of the thought of the Self, not thinned by thoughts of another kind, like the flame of a lamp in a windless place. Such a one, helped by the many restraints and observances, truth, brahmacarya, non-harming, giving up of possessions, renunciation, purity, contentment, freedom from deceit and the rest, keeps this vow for life. ‘Which’: there are many worlds to be won by knowledge and by rites; which of them does he win by this meditation on Om?

sanskrit.deva:
तस्मै स होवाच ।
एतद्वै सत्यकाम परं चापरं च ब्रह्म यदोंकारः ।
तस्माद्विद्वानेतेनैवायतनेनैकतरमन्वेति ॥ २ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
tasmai sa hovāca |
etad vai satyakāma paraṃ cāparaṃ ca brahma yad oṃkāraḥ |
tasmād vidvān etenaivāyatanenaikataram anveti || 2 ||

lines.iast: tasmai sa hovāca
etad vai satyakāma paraṃ cāparaṃ ca brahma yad oṃkāraḥ
lines.deva: एतद्वै सत्यकाम परं चापरं च ब्रह्म यदोंकारः

lines.iast: tasmād vidvān etenaivāyatanenaikataram anveti

padaccheda.iast: tasmai saḥ ha uvāca etat vai satyakāma param ca aparam ca brahma yat oṃkāraḥ tasmāt vidvān etena eva āyatanena ekataram anveti
padaccheda.deva: तस्मै सः ह उवाच एतत् वै सत्यकाम परम् च अपरम् च ब्रह्म यत् ओंकारः तस्मात् विद्वान् एतेन एव आयतनेन एकतरम् अन्वेति

translations.text: He said to him: ‘The syllable Om, Satyakāma, is Brahman, the higher and the lower. Therefore one who knows reaches, by this support alone, one or the other.’

notes: Śaṅkara: the higher Brahman is the true, the imperishable, called Puruṣa; the lower is that called prāṇa, the first-born. Om is that, has that for its self, because Om is its symbol. The higher Brahman cannot be pointed out by a word or the like, being free of every particular property, and, being beyond the reach of the senses, cannot be entered by the mind alone. But for those who meditate on Om, which stands in the place of an image of Viṣṇu or another, when the idea of Brahman has been laid on it by devotion, that Brahman is gracious: this is understood on the authority of scripture. So too with the lower Brahman. Therefore Om is spoken of, by a figure, as Brahman, the higher and the lower.
Śaṅkara: āyatana: the means of reaching the Self, the meditation on Om. By it one who knows thus reaches one or the other, the higher Brahman or the lower, for Om is the nearest support of Brahman.

sanskrit.deva:
स यद्येकमात्रमभिध्यायीत ।
स तेनैव संवेदितस्तूर्णमेव जगत्यामभिसम्पद्यते ।
तमृचो मनुष्यलोकमुपनयन्ते ।
स तत्र तपसा ब्रह्मचर्येण श्रद्धया सम्पन्नो महिमानमनुभवति ॥ ३ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
sa yady ekamātram abhidhyāyīta |
sa tenaiva saṃveditas tūrṇam eva jagatyām abhisampadyate |
tam ṛco manuṣyalokam upanayante |
sa tatra tapasā brahmacaryeṇa śraddhayā sampanno mahimānam anubhavati || 3 ||

lines.iast: sa yady ekamātram abhidhyāyīta
sa tenaiva saṃveditas tūrṇam eva jagatyām abhisampadyate
tam ṛco manuṣyalokam upanayante
sa tatra tapasā brahmacaryeṇa śraddhayā sampanno mahimānam anubhavati
lines.deva: स तत्र तपसा ब्रह्मचर्येण श्रद्धया सम्पन्नो महिमानमनुभवति

padaccheda.iast: saḥ yadi eka-mātram abhidhyāyīta saḥ tena eva saṃveditaḥ tūrṇam eva jagatyām abhisampadyate tam ṛcaḥ manuṣya-lokam upanayante saḥ tatra tapasā brahmacaryeṇa śraddhayā sampannaḥ mahimānam anubhavati
padaccheda.deva: सः यदि एक-मात्रम् अभिध्यायीत सः तेन एव संवेदितः तूर्णम् एव जगत्याम् अभिसम्पद्यते तम् ऋचः मनुष्य-लोकम् उपनयन्ते सः तत्र तपसा ब्रह्मचर्येण श्रद्धया सम्पन्नः महिमानम् अनुभवति

grammar.en: past passive participle m. nom. sg.
past passive participle m. nom. sg.

translations.text: If he meditates on it as of one measure, enlightened by that alone he quickly arrives on the earth. The ṛc verses bring him to the world of men. There, endowed with austerity, brahmacarya and faith, he experiences greatness.

notes: Śaṅkara: even if he does not know the division of all the measures of Om, by the power of the meditation on Om he goes to an excellent course; one whose refuge is Om does not, through the defect of knowing only a part, fall from both rites and knowledge and come to a bad end. If he knows the division of one measure only and meditates always on Om as of one measure, then, enlightened by that meditation alone, he quickly arrives on the earth. Many births are possible on the earth; of these the ṛc verses bring him to the world of men. There, in a human birth, as the best of the twice-born, endowed with austerity, brahmacarya and faith, he experiences greatness; he does not lose faith and act as he likes. One who has fallen from yoga never comes to a bad end.

sanskrit.deva:
अथ यदि द्विमात्रेण मनसि संपद्यते ।
सोऽन्तरीक्षं यजुर्भिरुन्नीयते सोमलोकम् ।
स सोमलोके विभूतिमनुभूय पुनरावर्तते ॥ ४ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
atha yadi dvimātreṇa manasi saṃpadyate |
so 'ntarīkṣaṃ yajurbhir unnīyate somalokam |
sa somaloke vibhūtim anubhūya punar āvartate || 4 ||

lines.iast: atha yadi dvimātreṇa manasi saṃpadyate
so 'ntarīkṣaṃ yajurbhir unnīyate somalokam
sa somaloke vibhūtim anubhūya punar āvartate

padaccheda.iast: atha yadi dvi-mātreṇa manasi saṃpadyate saḥ antarīkṣam yajurbhiḥ unnīyate soma-lokam saḥ soma-loke vibhūtim anubhūya punaḥ āvartate
padaccheda.deva: अथ यदि द्वि-मात्रेण मनसि संपद्यते सः अन्तरीक्षम् यजुर्भिः उन्नीयते सोम-लोकम् सः सोम-लोके विभूतिम् अनुभूय पुनः आवर्तते

words.meaning: to the world of the moon
in the world of the moon

translations.text: But if (he meditates on it) with two measures, he becomes one with the mind; he is led up by the yajus formulas to the sky, the world of the moon. Having experienced splendour in the world of the moon, he returns again.

notes: Śaṅkara: if, knowing the division of two measures, he meditates on Om as marked by two, he becomes one, through one-pointedness, with the mind: that which has the nature of dream, is to be thought on, is made of the Yajus and has Soma for its deity. Having become so and died, he is led up by the yajus formulas, which are the form of the second measure, to the sky, the support that is the form of the second measure, to the world of the moon: the sense is that the yajus bring him to a lunar birth. Having experienced splendour there he returns to the world of men.

sanskrit.deva:
यः पुनरेतं त्रिमात्रेणोमित्येतेनैवाक्षरेण परं पुरुषमभिध्यायीत ।
स तेजसि सूर्ये संपन्नः ।
यथा पादोदरस्त्वचा विनिर्मुच्यते ।
एवं ह वै स पाप्मना विनिर्मुक्तः स सामभिरुन्नीयते ब्रह्मलोकम् ।
स एतस्माज्जीवघनात्परात्परं पुरिशयं पुरुषमीक्षते तदेतौ श्लोकौ भवतः ॥ ५ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
yaḥ punar etaṃ trimātreṇomity etenaivākṣareṇa paraṃ puruṣam abhidhyāyīta |
sa tejasi sūrye saṃpannaḥ |
yathā pādodaras tvacā vinirmucyate |
evaṃ ha vai sa pāpmanā vinirmuktaḥ sa sāmabhir unnīyate brahmalokam |
sa etasmāj jīvaghanāt parāt paraṃ puriśayaṃ puruṣam īkṣate tad etau ślokau bhavataḥ || 5 ||

lines.iast: yaḥ punar etaṃ trimātreṇomity etenaivākṣareṇa paraṃ puruṣam abhidhyāyīta
sa tejasi sūrye saṃpannaḥ
yathā pādodaras tvacā vinirmucyate
evaṃ ha vai sa pāpmanā vinirmuktaḥ sa sāmabhir unnīyate brahmalokam
lines.deva: एवं ह वै स पाप्मना विनिर्मुक्तः स सामभिरुन्नीयते ब्रह्मलोकम्

lines.iast: sa etasmāj jīvaghanāt parāt paraṃ puriśayaṃ puruṣam īkṣate tad etau ślokau bhavataḥ
lines.deva: स एतस्माज्जीवघनात्परात्परं पुरिशयं पुरुषमीक्षते तदेतौ श्लोकौ भवतः

padaccheda.iast: yaḥ punaḥ etam tri-mātreṇa om iti etena eva akṣareṇa param puruṣam abhidhyāyīta saḥ tejasi sūrye saṃpannaḥ yathā pādodaraḥ tvacā vinirmucyate evam ha vai saḥ pāpmanā vinirmuktaḥ saḥ sāmabhiḥ unnīyate brahma-lokam saḥ etasmāt jīva-ghanāt parāt param puri-śayam puruṣam īkṣate tat etau ślokau bhavataḥ
padaccheda.deva: यः पुनः एतम् त्रि-मात्रेण ॐ इति एतेन एव अक्षरेण परम् पुरुषम् अभिध्यायीत सः तेजसि सूर्ये संपन्नः यथा पादोदरः त्वचा विनिर्मुच्यते एवम् ह वै सः पाप्मना विनिर्मुक्तः सः सामभिः उन्नीयते ब्रह्म-लोकम् सः एतस्मात् जीव-घनात् परात् परम् पुरि-शयम् पुरुषम् ईक्षते तत् एतौ श्लोकौ भवतः

past passive participle m. nom. sg.

translations.text: But he who meditates on the supreme Puruṣa by this very syllable Om of three measures is united with the light, the sun. As a snake is freed from its skin, so he is freed from sin. He is led up by the sāman chants to the world of Brahmā. He sees the Puruṣa who lies in the city (of the body), who is higher than this high mass of jīvas (Hiraṇyagarbha). On this there are these two verses:

notes: Śaṅkara: he who meditates on this Om, by means of the syllable Om with the knowledge of its three measures, as a symbol, on the supreme Puruṣa who is within the sun. That Om is a support as a symbol is the matter in hand, by the text that does not divide it from Brahman, higher and lower; and otherwise the accusative oṃkāram, heard many times, would be contradicted. Though the instrumental could stand, Om being the instrument of the meditation, yet, in keeping with the matter in hand, it is to be turned into the accusative, ‘the supreme Puruṣa of three measures’, by the rule ‘one should give up one for the sake of the family’.

Śaṅkara: he, in the form of the third measure, becomes united with the light, the sun; even when he has died meditating he does not return from the sun as from the world of the moon, but remains united with the sun. As a snake freed from its worn skin becomes new again, so he, freed from sin, the impurity that stands in the place of the snake's skin, is led upward by the sāman chants, which are the form of the third measure, to the world of Brahmā, of Hiraṇyagarbha, called Satya.

Śaṅkara: Hiraṇyagarbha is the Self of all the jīvas that are in saṃsāra, for in the form of the subtle body he is the inner self of all beings, and in him, the subtle self, all the jīvas are massed together: so he is the jīvaghana. The knower who knows Om of three measures sees, as he meditates, the Puruṣa called the supreme Self, higher than that high jīvaghana, Hiraṇyagarbha, lying in the city, that is, entered into all bodies.
The e-text reads jīvadhanāt parāparaṃ; it is set right here to jīvaghanāt parāt paraṃ, as the bhāṣya has it.

sanskrit.deva:
तिस्रो मात्रा मृत्युमत्यः प्रयुक्ता अन्योन्यसक्ता अनविप्रयुक्ताः ।
क्रियासु बाह्याभ्यन्तरमध्यमासु सम्यक्प्रयुक्तासु न कम्पते ज्ञः ॥ ६ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
tisro mātrā mṛtyumatyaḥ prayuktā anyonyasaktā anaviprayuktāḥ |
kriyāsu bāhyābhyantaramadhyamāsu samyakprayuktāsu na kampate jñaḥ || 6 ||

lines.iast: tisro mātrā mṛtyumatyaḥ prayuktā anyonyasaktā anaviprayuktāḥ
lines.deva: तिस्रो मात्रा मृत्युमत्यः प्रयुक्ता अन्योन्यसक्ता अनविप्रयुक्ताः

lines.iast: kriyāsu bāhyābhyantaramadhyamāsu samyakprayuktāsu na kampate jñaḥ
lines.deva: क्रियासु बाह्याभ्यन्तरमध्यमासु सम्यक्प्रयुक्तासु न कम्पते ज्ञः

padaccheda.iast: tisraḥ mātrāḥ mṛtyumatyaḥ prayuktāḥ anyonya-saktāḥ an-aviprayuktāḥ kriyāsu bāhya-ābhyantara-madhyamāsu samyak-prayuktāsu na kampate jñaḥ
padaccheda.deva: तिस्रः मात्राः मृत्युमत्यः प्रयुक्ताः अन्योन्य-सक्ताः अन्-अविप्रयुक्ताः क्रियासु बाह्य-आभ्यन्तर-मध्यमासु सम्यक्-प्रयुक्तासु न कम्पते ज्ञः

grammar.en: past passive participle f. nom. pl.

translations.text: The three measures are within the range of death. When they are employed joined to one another and not apart, in the outer, the inner and the middle acts (of meditation) rightly employed, the knower does not tremble.

notes: Śaṅkara: the three measures of Om are a, u and m. mṛtyumatyaḥ: they have death, they have not passed beyond the range of death. prayuktāḥ: employed in the acts of meditation on the Self; and joined to one another. Employed apart would be employed each on its own single object; they are not so employed. Rather, at one time of meditation, in the three acts, outer, inner and middle, the acts of yoga that are the meditation on the Puruṣa of the waking, the dreaming and the deep sleep state, when these are rightly employed, the yogin who knows the division of Om as told does not tremble, does not waver.

Śaṅkara: wavering is not possible for one who knows thus, for the Puruṣas of waking, dream and deep sleep, with their states, have been seen as the three measures, as Om itself. Having become the Self of all, made of Om, from where would he waver, or in what?

sanskrit.deva:
ऋग्भिरेतं यजुर्भिरन्तरिक्षं सामभिर्यत्तत्कवयो वेदयन्ते ।
तमोंकारेणैवायतनेनान्वेति विद्वान्यत्तच्छान्तमजरममृतमभयं परं चेति ॥ ७ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
ṛgbhir etaṃ yajurbhir antarikṣaṃ sāmabhir yat tat kavayo vedayante |
tam oṃkāreṇaivāyatanenānveti vidvān yat tac chāntam ajaram amṛtam abhayaṃ paraṃ ceti || 7 ||

lines.iast: ṛgbhir etaṃ yajurbhir antarikṣaṃ sāmabhir yat tat kavayo vedayante
tam oṃkāreṇaivāyatanenānveti vidvān yat tac chāntam ajaram amṛtam abhayaṃ paraṃ ceti

padaccheda.iast: ṛgbhiḥ etam yajurbhiḥ antarikṣam sāmabhiḥ yat tat kavayaḥ vedayante tam oṃkāreṇa eva āyatanena anveti vidvān yat tat śāntam ajaram amṛtam abhayam param ca iti
padaccheda.deva: ऋग्भिः एतम् यजुर्भिः अन्तरिक्षम् सामभिः यत् तत् कवयः वेदयन्ते तम् ओंकारेण एव आयतनेन अन्वेति विद्वान् यत् तत् शान्तम् अजरम् अमृतम् अभयम् परम् च इति

translations.text: By the ṛc verses this world, by the yajus formulas the sky, by the sāman chants that which the wise know (the world of Brahmā): that one who knows reaches with the syllable Om alone as support, and also that which is calm, ageless, deathless, fearless and supreme.

notes: Śaṅkara, introducing the mantra: the second verse gathers up the whole sense.

Śaṅkara: by the ṛc verses this world, marked by men; by the yajus the sky, over which Soma presides; by the sāman chants that third which the wise, only those who have knowledge, know as the world of Brahmā. That threefold world, which is the lower Brahman, one who knows reaches with Om as the means. By the same Om he reaches also that higher Brahman, the imperishable, the true, called Puruṣa: calm, free, without the whole spread of particulars such as waking, dream and deep sleep; therefore ageless and deathless; and, since it is without the change that is ageing, fearless; and, since fearless, supreme, unsurpassed. The word iti marks the end of the sentence.
